cosy-lesson.title: Without Love You Can Save the World

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Distraction – A thing that prevents someone from giving full attention to something else.

p.em: Example: The characters discover that romantic obsession is a massive, time-consuming distraction.

cosy-blockquote.p: Productivity – The effectiveness of productive effort, especially in industry or personal life.

p.em: Example: Without romantic drama, Rebecca's daily productivity skyrockets to extraordinary levels.

cosy-blockquote.p: Obsession – An unhealthy idea or thought that continually preoccupies or intrudes on a mind.

p.em: Example: Chasing romance felt like a full-time job driven by obsessive energy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Potential – Having or showing the capacity to become or develop into something in the future.

p.em: Example: Free from love, they realize they have the potential to solve global crises.

cosy-blockquote.p: Focus – The center of interest or activity; intense mental effort on a goal.

p.em: Example: Redirecting romantic focus into career and charity leads to remarkable results.

cosy-blockquote.p: Freedom – The power or right to act, speak, or think as one wants without hindrance.

p.em: Example: Singlehood gives them total personal freedom to manage their schedules.

cosy-blockquote.p: Achievement – A thing done successfully with effort, skill, or courage.

p.em: Example: Building a house for charity is a concrete achievement made possible by single life.

cosy-blockquote.p: Priorities – Things that are regarded as more important than others.

p.em: Example: Removing dating drama forces them to reevaluate their life priorities.

cosy-blockquote.p: Energy – The strength and vitality required for sustained physical or mental activity.

p.em: Example: Romantic longing drains emotional energy that could be spent on noble causes.

cosy-blockquote.p: Liberation – The act of setting someone free from imprisonment, slavery, or oppression.

p.em: Example: Giving up on love feels like an unexpected form of personal liberation.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: Without love you can to save the world → Correct: Without love you can save the world ((Use bare infinitive 'save' after modal verb 'can'.))
Incorrect: She is focused in her career → Correct: She is focused on her career ((Use 'focused on'.))
Incorrect: He has more time for build a house → Correct: He has more time to build a house ((Use 'time to + infinitive'.))
